body: The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)

options.text: receives data from the application as a single stream only
does all of the above: is connection-oriented, takes application data as a stream and uses a three-way handshake
options.hint: Correct. All three are true of TCP.
True, but not the only correct statement.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

TCP is **connection-oriented** (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK three-way handshake), **byte-stream** oriented and reliable (sequencing, acknowledgement, retransmission, flow control).

## Simplified explanation

All of them.

body: Which of the following bears the characteristics of an **analog** quantity?

options.text: It has a continuous set of values over a given range
It is described with a finite number of steps

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Analog signals vary **continuously** and can take infinitely many values in a range; digital signals take a **finite** set of discrete values.

## Simplified explanation

Continuous = analog.

body: Synchronisation **without increasing the number of bits** is provided by

options.hint: Correct. E.g. B8ZS, HDB3 substitute patterns for long zero runs.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Block coding (4B/5B) adds bits to guarantee transitions; **scrambling** (B8ZS, HDB3) replaces long runs of zeros with violation patterns, so it keeps synchronisation **without increasing bit count**.

## Simplified explanation

**Scrambling**.

body: Which of the following is **not** a service carried by ISDN?

options.hint: Correct. ISDN carries data, voice and video.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

ISDN (Integrated Services Digital Network) integrates **voice, data and video** over digital lines.

## Simplified explanation

It carries them all.

body: A beam of light travels through media of two different densities. If the angle of incidence is greater than the **critical angle**, what occurs?

options.hint: Correct. Total internal reflection: the principle of optical fibre.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Below the critical angle light refracts; at it, it grazes the boundary; above it, **total internal reflection** occurs. This keeps light inside the fibre core.

## Simplified explanation

Greater than critical → **reflection**.

body: Which term refers to the **structure or format** of the data, i.e. the order in which they are presented?
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

A protocol's three key elements: **syntax** (format), **semantics** (meaning), **timing** (when and how fast data is sent).

## Simplified explanation

Format = **syntax**.

body: A transmission impairment in which the signal **loses strength** due to the resistance of the medium is

options.hint: Correct. Loss of energy; amplifiers/repeaters compensate.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Impairments: **attenuation** (loss of strength, measured in dB), **distortion** (shape change from differing propagation speeds), **noise** (thermal, induced, crosstalk, impulse).

## Simplified explanation

Weaker = **attenuation**.

body: Special-interest groups that test, evaluate and standardise **new technologies** are called

options.hint: Correct. E.g. Frame Relay Forum, ATM Forum.
Government bodies such as the FCC/NCA.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Forouzan: **forums** are formed by industry and users to speed up the acceptance of new technologies, then present their conclusions to standards bodies.

## Simplified explanation

**Forum**.

body: Which topology requires a **multipoint** connection?

options.hint: Correct. All devices share one backbone.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

A **bus** uses one long cable to which all nodes are tapped: a multipoint line. Mesh, star and ring use point-to-point links.

## Simplified explanation

Shared cable = **bus**.

body: Which network was originally designed for **data** communication?

options.hint: Correct. The telephone network was designed for voice.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The **telephone network** was built for **voice**; the **Internet** (ARPANET) was built for **data**.

## Simplified explanation

Data → Internet.

body: Why did the ISO develop the OSI model?

options.text: The rate of data transfer was increasing exponentially
Standards were needed to allow any two systems to communicate

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

OSI (1970s/80s) is a 7-layer **reference model** to let **any two different systems** communicate regardless of architecture.

## Simplified explanation

Interoperability.

body: The **bandwidth** of a network refers to

options.text: the transmission capacity of a communication link
options.hint: Correct. Bits per second it can carry.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Bandwidth = range of frequencies (Hz) or, in data terms, the **maximum bit rate** (bps) of a link.

## Simplified explanation

Capacity.

body: Comparing parallel and serial transmission, which is true?

options.text: Serial is used for long distances; parallel for short distances
Parallel transmission is faster than serial
Parallel transmission is costly compared to serial

options.hint: Correct. All three statements are true.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Parallel sends n bits at once over n wires (fast, costly, short distance); serial sends one bit at a time over one channel (cheaper, long distance).

## Simplified explanation

All.

body: The ISDN **D channel** carries network-service (signalling) information between the
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

ISDN: **B (bearer)** channels at 64 kbps carry user data/voice; the **D (data)** channel carries **signalling between user and network**.

## Simplified explanation

D = user ↔ network signalling.

body: Which of the following is **not** a traditional switching method?

options.hint: Correct. All three are traditional methods.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Traditional switching methods: **circuit**, **packet** (datagram/virtual circuit) and **message** switching.

## Simplified explanation

None.

body: Geostationary satellites

options.text: are normally placed in an orbit about 36,000 km from the earth's surface
are simplex with regard to data flow
do not rotate with the speed of the earth
options.hint: They match it, so they appear fixed.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

A geostationary satellite orbits at ≈36,000 km above the equator with a period of 24 h, so it appears stationary.

## Simplified explanation

36,000 km.

body: Which topology relies on a **central controller or hub**?

options.hint: Correct. All devices connect to the hub.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

In a **star**, every device has a dedicated link to a central hub/switch; if the hub fails the whole network fails.

## Simplified explanation

Hub = **star**.

body: The interface between a **user** and an **ATM switch** is the
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

ATM: **UNI** connects user equipment to a switch; **NNI** connects switches to each other.

## Simplified explanation

User → **UNI**.

body: The IP is a(n) ______ datagram protocol.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

IP provides **best-effort** (unreliable), **connectionless** delivery; reliability is left to TCP.

## Simplified explanation

Both.

body: Which of the following describes **modulation**?

options.text: Varying some characteristic of a carrier wave in accordance with an information-carrying signal
Conversion of digital signal to digital data
Conversion of digital data to digital signal

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Modulation (AM, FM, PM; ASK, FSK, PSK, QAM) varies a carrier's **amplitude, frequency or phase** with the message.

## Simplified explanation

Varying a carrier.

body: The **session, presentation and application** layers of the OSI model together correspond to which TCP/IP layer?

options.hint: Correct. TCP/IP has one application layer.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

TCP/IP's **application layer** covers OSI layers 5–7.

## Simplified explanation

**Application**.

body: The set of procedures used to restrict the amount of data a sender can send before waiting for acknowledgement is
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

**Flow control** (stop-and-wait, sliding window) limits data sent before acknowledgement; **error control** handles detection and retransmission.

## Simplified explanation

**Flow**.

body: Which method(s) can be used to move data through a network?
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Data can traverse a network by **circuit switching** (dedicated path) or **packet switching** (independent packets).

## Simplified explanation

Both.

body: The TCP is a ______ protocol.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

TCP sets up a connection before data transfer; UDP is connectionless.

## Simplified explanation

**Connection-oriented**.

body: Transmission media lie directly **below** which layer?
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Transmission media (cables, air) sit **below the physical layer**, which controls them.

## Simplified explanation

**Physical**.

body: Which of the following is **not** a form of data used in communication?

options.hint: Correct. All are forms of data.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Data forms: **text, numbers, images, audio, video**.

## Simplified explanation

None.

body: Which layer **establishes, maintains and synchronises** the interaction between communicating devices?
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

OSI layer 5, **session**: dialog control (half/full duplex) and synchronisation (checkpoints).

## Simplified explanation

**Session**.

body: The measure a routing algorithm uses to determine the optimal path to a destination is the

options.hint: Correct. Hop count, cost, delay, bandwidth.

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Routing protocols assign a **metric** (cost) to each path and choose the lowest.

## Simplified explanation

**Metric**.

body: Which is a characteristic of data communication?

options.text: All of the above: delivery, accuracy and timeliness

explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Effectiveness depends on **delivery**, **accuracy**, **timeliness** (and **jitter**).

## Simplified explanation

All.

body: Which of the following is a possible **encoding/conversion** process?
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Four conversions: digital→digital (line coding), analog→digital (PCM), digital→analog (shift keying), analog→analog (AM/FM/PM).

## Simplified explanation

All.

body: (a) Define **computer network**. (b) Distinguish between (i) data and information; (ii) parallel and serial transmission.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** A computer network is a set of **computers and devices (nodes) interconnected by communication links** to share resources and exchange data.
>
> **(b)(i)** **Data** are raw, unprocessed facts (e.g. marks 45, 67); **information** is data **processed** into a meaningful form (e.g. class average 56).
>
> **(ii)** **Parallel**: several bits (e.g. 8) sent **simultaneously** over multiple wires; fast but costly and short-distance. **Serial**: bits sent **one after another** over a single channel; cheaper, used for long distances (can be asynchronous or synchronous).
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Know the definition precisely and give an example for each contrast.

## Simplified explanation

Linked computers; raw vs processed; many wires vs one.
hint: Give the points with a brief explanation each.

body: With the aid of a diagram, discuss the **mesh** topology and give **two** of its disadvantages.
answer:
> [!answer]
> In a **mesh** topology every device has a **dedicated point-to-point link to every other device**. For n devices, the number of links = **n(n−1)/2** (each device has n−1 I/O ports). (Diagram: e.g. 4 nodes each joined to the other 3: 6 links.)
>
> **Advantages:** dedicated links (no traffic sharing), robust (one link failure doesn't stop the network), privacy/security, easy fault isolation.
>
> **Disadvantages:** (1) **large amount of cabling** and many I/O ports: expensive; (2) **difficult installation and reconfiguration**; (3) bulky wiring takes space.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Quote the link formula n(n−1)/2.

## Simplified explanation

Everyone linked to everyone; costly cabling.
hint: Give the points with a brief explanation each.

body: (a) Discuss the **three** characteristics essential to any data communication system. (b)(i) Give **five** advantages of optical fibre over twisted-pair and coaxial cable. (ii) Distinguish between **simplex** and **full-duplex** transmission.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** (1) **Delivery**: data must reach the correct destination/user. (2) **Accuracy**: data must arrive without alteration/errors. (3) **Timeliness**: data must be delivered on time (real-time for audio/video). (Also **jitter**: uneven packet arrival time.)
>
> **(b)(i)** (1) **Higher bandwidth**/data rate; (2) **less attenuation**, so longer distances between repeaters; (3) **immune to electromagnetic interference**; (4) resistant to corrosive materials; (5) **light weight**; (6) more **secure** (hard to tap).
>
> **(ii)** **Simplex**: communication in **one direction only** (keyboard → computer, TV broadcast). **Full duplex**: both stations send and receive **simultaneously** (telephone).
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Half-duplex (walkie-talkie) is the in-between mode: both directions but not at the same time.

## Simplified explanation

Delivery, accuracy, timeliness; fibre = fast, far, interference-free.
hint: Give the points with a brief explanation each.
